title: Dark Shrouds in Orion
caption: The dark nebula LDN 1622, imaged by the Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope
celestial: LDN 1622 · constellation Orion · about 1300 light-years away (source figure)
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/T. A. Rector. Image processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab) & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Shadowy clouds spread across this image of LDN 1622, a dark nebula. Dense clouds of gas and dust like this blot out the light of objects behind them, so they appear as ink-dark shapes against a backdrop of stars.

At a distance of 1300 light-years, LDN 1622 belongs to the nearby Orion complex, a star-forming area crowded with young stars and other dark nebulae. The picture was taken in 2018 with Mosaic-3, a wide-field camera on Kitt Peak National Observatory's Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope in Arizona, built for covering large stretches of the night sky.

Mosaic-3 has since been retired to make room for the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), described as the world's most powerful multi-object survey spectrograph. The swap shows one advantage of telescopes on the ground: instruments can be upgraded or replaced as new technology arrives. This observation was made before the 2022 Contreras Fire, which affected Kitt Peak.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (36.59 x 37.59 arcminutes) and distance (1300 light years), the frame spans roughly 14 × 14 light-years. Its light set out about 1,300 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with the Mosaic-3 camera on the NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope through g, i and hydrogen-alpha filters; the colour mapping isn't published.
